audit_findings.title: FY2025 owner earnings do not contain the current debt structure’s full interest burden
audit_findings.magnitude: $31.0625m annual stated-note coupon; 1H2026 interest expense was $10.464m above 1H2025
audit_findings.mechanism: The equity-level OE forecast retains interest expense, so the anchor must include the recurring interest burden associated with the current debt structure.
audit_findings.evidence: On November 5, 2025, the Company, as issuer, completed an issuance of $350.0 million aggregate principal amount of 8.875% senior unsecured notes at 96.0% of par with stated maturity on November 5, 2029 (the “2029 Senior Notes”) pursuant to a note purchase agreement (the “Note Purchase Agreement”).
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated timing mismatch. The $350m notes were issued on November 5, 2025, so FY2025 included only a short interest stub, while the valuation uses the June 2026 capital structure. The annual note coupon alone is many times the negative $0.9m anchor and comparable to the entire stated equity value of $29m-$36m. The precise adjustment remains unresolved because revolver refinancing, discount amortization, and earnings from subsequently financed assets must be matched.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct pro forma FY2025 OE using a full year of note coupon, original-issue-discount and financing-cost amortization, and June 2026 revolver interest; separately add only cash earnings attributable to assets absent from FY2025, then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Negative-anchor growth mechanically reverses the scenario meanings
audit_findings.magnitude: $7m or $0.05 per share between the stated bear and bull values
audit_findings.mechanism: Growth is applied directly to negative OE, causing higher growth assumptions to deepen losses and reduce operating PV and equity value; the negative amount also flows into terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Because of normal production declines, increased or decreased drilling activities, fluctuations in commodity prices and the effects of acquisitions and divestitures, the historical information presented below should not be interpreted as being indicative of future results.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated model error: bear, base, and bull values decline from $0.27 to $0.24 to $0.22 as growth improves from -5% to 3% to 6%. Thus the scenario labels do not represent economic downside and upside. More importantly, perpetuating unrecovered negative OE does not produce a decision-useful going-concern value. The $7m displayed inversion understates the possible effect because a supportable return to positive normalized OE could change both forecast cash flows and terminal value.
audit_findings.action: Do not rely on the stated valuation conclusion. Establish a filed-data-supported normalization and explicit path to positive OE, with scenario ordering constraints, or classify the company as unvalued/too hard and omit intrinsic-value and buy-below outputs.

audit_findings.title: Decommissioning obligations may be an unmodeled claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $12.720m recorded ARO at December 31, 2025; $26.5m net abandonment costs included in filed reserve PV-10
audit_findings.mechanism: Future plugging and abandonment cash payments must enter maintenance capital or be deducted as an equity-value claim; adding back noncash accretion without recognizing settlements would overstate OE.
audit_findings.evidence: We accrue a liability for decommissioning costs associated with our operators' wells but have not established any cash reserve account for these potential costs in respect of any of the Properties.
audit_findings.explanation: The obligation is demonstrated, although its treatment in the OE calculation is unresolved. The booked ARO equals roughly 35%-44% of the stated $29m-$36m equity values, while the reserve report’s $26.5m abandonment-cost estimate equals roughly 74%-91%. Those scales make a possible omission material. The reserve PV-10 disclosure does not by itself establish that this separate OE DCF includes the costs.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile beginning ARO, liabilities incurred, accretion, revisions, and cash settlements to the OE schedule; compare the expected undiscounted abandonment schedule with maintenance capital and deduct any uncovered amount once, avoiding duplication with reserve-based cash flows.

audit_findings.title: The anchor predates a contractual increase in recurring management expense
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.75m annual minimum increase from $10.0m to $11.75m; up to $2.5m before CPI adjustments; 1H2026 service fees increased by $0.9m year over year
audit_findings.mechanism: The recurring fee reduces forecast OE beginning in 2026 and CPI adjustments affect later forecast and terminal-period margins.
audit_findings.evidence: Amendment No. 1, among other things, (a) extended the initial term from April 30, 2028 to April 30, 2031 and (b) increased the Services Fee (as defined in MSA) from $ 10.0 million to $ 11.75 million effective January 1, 2026, provided for annual CPI-based adjustments beginning January 1, 2027 and delegated to management the authority to increase the Services Fee up to a maximum total of $ 12.5 million.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated forecast omission unless an explicit adjustment exists outside the supplied model. The minimum $1.75m annual increase is nearly twice the absolute $0.9m anchor, and the authorized $12.5m fee plus CPI escalation can widen the difference. Applying generic growth to FY2025 net OE does not capture this contractual cost step-up.
audit_findings.action: Adjust normalized OE for the $11.75m 2026 fee, test the authorized $12.5m level, apply contract-consistent CPI escalation from 2027, and rerun the valuation after correcting the negative-anchor methodology.

audit_findings.title: The new power contract creates fixed future payments absent from FY2025 operations
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; related net derivative asset was $1.438m at June 30, 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Fixed capacity payments and variable operating-profit receipts enter forecast OE; any net derivative asset or liability also affects the equity bridge if the same contractual cash flows are not already captured in OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Under the arrangement, the Company is obligated to make fixed monthly payments based on operating generation capacity multiplied by its participation interest.
audit_findings.explanation: The contract and its seven-year future settlement exposure are demonstrated, but the filed record does not disclose enough information to quantify the gross fixed payments or expected net cash flows. The June 2026 fair-value asset is only a net estimate based on significant unobservable assumptions and cannot substitute for an OE forecast. Outcomes may raise or lower value depending on power prices, gas costs, facility timing, operating efficiency, and performance.
audit_findings.action: Obtain participation capacity, fixed monthly rate, operating-and-maintenance charge, commercial-operation schedule, and downside protections; model gross receipts and payments by year, reconcile the result to the $1.438m Level 3 fair value, and ensure the contract is counted either in OE or the bridge but not both.

audit_findings.title: The near-zero anchor may retain nonrecurring transition and financing costs
audit_findings.magnitude: up to the $6.360m increase in 2025 total G&A over 2024; exact severance and capital-markets amounts are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Removing genuinely nonrecurring cash expenses increases normalized OE, while excluding recurring replacement compensation or continuing financing costs would improperly increase OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase was primarily due to severance expense incurred during the period as a result of a management transition as well as expenses related to capital market activities.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that severance and capital-market activities contributed materially to the G&A increase, but does not disaggregate their amounts or establish their treatment in the supplied OE calculation. The total $6.360m G&A increase is more than seven times the absolute $0.9m anchor and equals roughly 18%-22% of stated equity value, so the potential normalization is reasonably capable of changing the valuation. The net direction remains mixed until recurring replacement and financing costs are separated.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the general-ledger or footnote breakdown for severance, capital-market costs, replacement compensation, legal fees, and financing costs; trace each item into OE, remove only evidenced nonrecurring cash charges, retain recurring costs, and rerun the corrected model.
